newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Capital Intelligence lifts Moroccan bank.
newsitem.headline: Capital Intelligence lifts Moroccan bank.

text.p: The Cyprus-based Capital Intelligence specialist bank rating service said on Monday it had raised the long-term rating of Morocco's Banque Commerciale du Maroc to BBB+ (BBB plus) from BBB.
In a statement sent to Reuters, it said the short-term rating was re-affirmed at A-2 "and a stable outlook has been assigned".
Capital Intelligence added: "In recent years, the bank has adopted a strategy of diversification with the creation of several associated companies which specialise in a variety of financial services.
"It is also further developing its international business, an area which has long been dominated by Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur."
The rating service said Banque Commerciale du Maroc had a highly lucrative franchise and "key financial indicators are sound."

The bank's track record had been impressive and it was "in a good position to retain its market share over the long term and well equipped to face the challenge of Morocco's financial sector deregulation."
"With total assets of $3.6 billion at end 1995, BCM is Morocco's third largest bank," the rating service said.
The main shareholders are the Moroccan private conglomerate ONA Group and the Spanish group Banco Central Hispano Americano.
One of the 46 listed stocks on the Casablanca bourse BCM was lasted traded at 685 dirhams.
